── OWNER RULING 2026-09-30 ~01:35Z on OWN-084 / OWN-088 (multiple choice, recorded by HYG-156, ADR-1672): the second provider is "Cloudflare R2". The copy job reads its target from exactly these four env vars, set on Vercel Production by the owner (OWN-088), and no other names: R2_ACCOUNT_ID (the <id> in <id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com), R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID, R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and R2_BACKUP_BUCKET (bucket frequency-storage-backup). These are the names the build branch for this row already reads (lib/backup/r2.ts on claude/hyg-144-storage-backup-r2). Because they live on Vercel, the job takes the Vercel cron form of the two options above. Until they exist it fails dark and says so. The closing test is unchanged.

CLOSED 2026-09-30. ADR-1693. PREMISE RE-TESTED (ADR-1082) on main at fb91c7b48: no backup code, no R2 or S3 client, no S3-signing dependency; OWN-082's rehearsal had shown the database backup restores storage.objects rows (526) and not the files. Built on the owner rulings OWN-084 "Nightly copy elsewhere" and backup store "Cloudflare R2".

WHAT SHIPPED. app/api/cron/storage-backup (vercel.json 20 5 * * *; withCronHeartbeat; cronBudget(500); maxDuration 300; CRON_FRESHNESS daily; CRON_UNMONITORED with the note that the owner adds a check and moves it to CRON_MONITORED, since all 20 Healthchecks slots are taken). lib/backup/storage-copy.ts: lists objects in every bucket changed strictly after the cursor through public.backup_storage_objects_since (migration 20270345010400, SECURITY INVOKER, revoked from anon and authenticated, service_role only, pgTAP supabase/tests/backup_storage_objects_since.test.sql), streams each through a signed URL to an R2 PUT keyed <bucket>/<path>, and writes the platform_settings cursor storage_backup_cursor after every object; caps 500 objects, 1.5 GiB and the 240 s clock per run, the first object always taken; a failed copy stops with the cursor on the last success and answers 500. lib/backup/r2.ts + lib/backup/sigv4.ts: a node:crypto SigV4 signer pinned to three AWS published S3 examples, UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD, no SDK. Inert until R2_ACCOUNT_ID, R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID, R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and R2_BACKUP_BUCKET are all set (blank in .env.example): logs cron.storage_backup.inert and creates no database client. docs/RUNBOOKS.md section 7: restore one file or a bucket from R2.

NOT YET MEASURED. No run has copied a file: the owner creates the bucket and token and sets the four variables (OWN-088). The probe measures the wiring and the signer, not a copy in production.

verify.note: Reads the tree: vercel.json schedules /api/cron/storage-backup; the route is behind the cron bearer and withCronHeartbeat("storage-backup") and checks the R2 config before it creates the admin client; lib/backup/r2.ts reads all four R2 variables (each blank in .env.example) and PUTs through fetch with a SigV4-signed request to <account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com; the copy loop lists through backup_storage_objects_since and, per object, checks the clock and byte cap, PUTs, then writes the cursor; keys are <bucket>/<path>; a migration defines the function over storage.objects in (changed_at, id) order and revokes it from public, anon, authenticated; scripts/function-grants.txt records it internal; slos.ts declares the job; RUNBOOKS has the R2 restore section naming OWN-088. Then loads lib/backup/sigv4.ts under type stripping and reproduces AWS published GET Object signature (f0e8bdb8...) and RFC 3986 segment encoding. Fails on main at the schedule. Mutation-fired, each arm: path renamed in vercel.json; heartbeat job renamed; admin client created before the config check; the bucket variable renamed; a secret placeholder in .env.example; the fetch method POST; the per-object cursor write removed; the clock check removed; keys without the bucket; the order by id removed; the revoke narrowed to public; the grant ledger line removed; the partition entry renamed; the runbook heading renamed; the signing scope misspelt; the RFC 3986 extra characters dropped.
